title: Heap allocation in tight loops
summary: Allocating with new, make_unique, vector growth, or temporary containers repeatedly in hot loops.
rationale: Repeated allocation fragments memory and adds allocator contention in high-throughput paths.

detection.notes: Find allocations inside loops, callbacks, render paths, or packet/message processing.

impact.notes: Impact increases in hot paths, large inputs, high-concurrency services, build pipelines, or repeated request paths.

remediation.guidance: Reserve capacity, reuse buffers, use stack allocation, arenas, object pools, or move allocation outside the loop.
remediation.tradeoffs: Pools and arenas require lifecycle discipline and can increase retained memory.
